item.text: {"chapter_id":"7B","shard_id":"7B-S01","reviewed_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0003-E017","BATCH-0003-E019","BATCH-0003-E020","BATCH-0004-E004","BATCH-0004-E007","BATCH-0004-E008","BATCH-0004-E009","BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0004-E013","BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0004-E020","BATCH-0005-E003","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0005-E007","BATCH-0005-E008","BATCH-0005-E010","BATCH-0006-E007","BATCH-0007-E002","BATCH-0007-E005","BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0008-E007","BATCH-0008-E009","BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0008-E011","BATCH-0008-E012","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0009-E005","BATCH-0009-E006","BATCH-0009-E007","BATCH-0009-E008","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0009-E011","BATCH-0009-E012","BATCH-0010-E001","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0010-E004","BATCH-0010-E011","BATCH-0011-E008","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0012-E005","BATCH-0012-E009","BATCH-0012-E011","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E004","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0014-E006","BATCH-0014-E009"],"answers":[{"question_id":"7B.1","answer":"The shard contains repeated ruler-specific allegations or findings of inaccurate, misleading, or unsupported public representations. López Obrador repeatedly claimed that missing-person figures were exaggerated for political harm; later official totals were lower after a census whose methodology civil-society groups disputed. He denied or minimized Pegasus surveillance, first denying government use and later characterizing acknowledged military use as lawful intelligence rather than spying, despite forensic and documentary reporting. He also denied or rejected GIEI findings on Ayotzinapa and framed them as an unfounded campaign against the Army. The record includes contrary or qualifying material: the government created investigative bodies, issued or supported information-access commitments, and the SFP closed one conflict-of-interest inquiry for insufficient evidence. Several adverse claims concern agencies or associates rather than proven personal presidential deception.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0006-E007","BATCH-0007-E002","BATCH-0008-E012","BATCH-0009-E007","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0010-E001","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0014-E006","BATCH-0014-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E016"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not establish a final judicial finding that López Obrador personally intended each disputed statement to deceive.","Some claims are advocacy, journalistic, or expert allegations; several concern inherited or institutional conduct rather than the president personally."]},{"question_id":"7B.2","answer":"The shard shows limited correction and repeated disputed responses after adverse evidence. López Obrador acknowledged some Pegasus use but denied illegality, denied Army responsibility for surveillance of Alejandro Encinas, and told Encinas not to give it importance. He rejected GIEI findings rather than accepting their account. He announced a revised disappearance census after disputing the existing figures; the resulting lower total intensified concerns about concealment rather than resolving the underlying dispute. In the Ayotzinapa matter, the government initially created commissions, appointed investigators, and ordered cooperation, and some investigations and prosecutions proceeded, but military institutions were reported to have withheld records despite presidential requests. A separate 2023 government effort sought recovery of alleged corruption proceeds from a prior administration.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E008","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0009-E007","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0010-E001","BATCH-0010-E004","BATCH-0010-E011","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0014-E006","BATCH-0012-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E004","BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0012-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence does not show a complete presidential correction, remedy, or final accountability outcome for the principal disputed claims.","Military noncompliance is documented, but personal presidential knowledge, control, and response after notice remain partly unresolved."]},{"question_id":"7B.3","answer":"The shard contains a formal 2019 memorandum rejecting family business with government, but multiple later reports describe potential conflicts involving the president’s sons, relatives, associates, and contractors. These include the Baker Hughes-linked residence, contracts involving friends of Andrés López Beltrán, contracts involving a presidential cousin, and alleged access through family networks. López Obrador publicly denied conflicts and defended relatives. An SFP inquiry into the Casa Gris-related allegations concluded for lack of evidence, while expressly lacking jurisdiction over some foreign or non-federal conduct. The evidence therefore mixes a stated safeguard and an exculpatory administrative disposition with recurring allegations and disputed denials.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0007-E002","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0008-E011","BATCH-0009-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0008-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No supplied record establishes a final legal finding that López Obrador personally violated a conflict-of-interest rule.","Most alleged interests concern family members or associates; personal direction, recusal, divestment, and complete disclosure are not fully documented."]},{"question_id":"7B.4","answer":"The shard reports repeated alleged family and associate benefits connected to public contracts, contractor-linked housing, Pemex, SEDATU, health procurement, Dos Bocas, Tren Maya, Sembrando Vida, and other projects. It also records cash received by López Obrador’s brothers in videos and a prosecutorial decision not to pursue one brother for an electoral offense, pending judicial confirmation; the source does not establish presidential personal benefit. The SFP closed the Casa Gris-related inquiry for lack of sufficient evidence, but its jurisdiction was limited. Segalmex diversion was publicly acknowledged by López Obrador in December 2023, although the supplied accountability publication disputes his claim that it was the only corruption case and says warning signs existed since 2019. Some broader government enforcement and recovery efforts are favorable or mixed.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E003","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0006-E007","BATCH-0007-E002","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0008-E007","BATCH-0008-E011","BATCH-0009-E008","BATCH-0012-E011","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0012-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0013-E014"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard contains no final finding that López Obrador personally enriched himself or personally directed the alleged family transactions.","Several reports are advocacy or secondary summaries and expressly preserve allegations rather than adjudicated corruption."]},{"question_id":"7B.5","answer":"The shard reports concerns that appointments and access reflected loyalty, family, or political connection rather than competence or independent process. Examples include alleged inexperienced appointments of former presidential aides, concerns over a new National Search Commission head’s experience and recruitment transparency, alleged influence by the president’s son over appointments, and appointments or support for politically aligned officials and institutions. The record also shows independent or corrective appointments and functioning institutions, including a respected Ayotzinapa prosecutor and initial independent expert involvement, although those arrangements later weakened or stalled.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E007","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0008-E009","BATCH-0009-E008","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E016"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E017","BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not provide a comprehensive appointment-by-appointment record or definitive proof that López Obrador personally selected officials for self-dealing.","Some appointment criticisms concern agencies, legislatures, or state governments rather than direct presidential removals or appointments."]},{"question_id":"7B.6","answer":"The shard documents an initially meaningful investigative architecture for Ayotzinapa: a truth commission, a special prosecutor, independent experts, presidential orders to cooperate, and reported access agreements. It also documents repeated weakening or obstruction of independent scrutiny: military agencies allegedly withheld or denied records, investigators left after concluding cooperation was impossible, prosecutors resigned amid interference, transparency institutions lost quorum or were weakened, and the president attacked or discredited critics and organizations. The SFP investigation and some prosecution or recovery efforts provide contrary evidence that formal investigative mechanisms remained available in some matters.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E007","BATCH-0004-E008","BATCH-0004-E009","BATCH-0004-E020","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0008-E009","BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0009-E006","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0009-E011","BATCH-0010-E001","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0010-E011","BATCH-0011-E008","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0012-E005","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E004","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0014-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0012-E011","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most obstruction is attributed to military, prosecutorial, legislative, or administrative institutions; the shard does not establish personal presidential authorization for each act.","Formal mandates and orders are sometimes documented without complete implementation evidence."]},{"question_id":"7B.7","answer":"The shard contains substantial evidence of noncompliance, concealment, and pressure: military refusal or failure to provide Ayotzinapa records despite presidential requests; altered, moved, destroyed, or denied historical files; failure to register military detentions; noncompliance with transparency obligations; executive orders designed to exempt projects from transparency requirements; vetoes or blockage affecting INAI quorum; and public attacks on courts, investigators, journalists, and civil-society critics. The president also denied or minimized Pegasus allegations and GIEI findings. Contrary evidence includes initial cooperation agreements, some prosecutions, a government recovery lawsuit, court decisions permitting continued INAI operation, and official investigations of security personnel.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E004","BATCH-0004-E007","BATCH-0004-E008","BATCH-0004-E009","BATCH-0004-E020","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0009-E007","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0009-E011","BATCH-0010-E001","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0010-E011","BATCH-0011-E008","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0012-E011","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E004","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0014-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0012-E011","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E016"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Some reported obstruction is institutional and cannot be assigned personally to López Obrador on the supplied evidence.","Allegations, expert conclusions, and ongoing investigations are not equivalent to final judicial findings."]},{"question_id":"7B.8","answer":"The shard shows a mixed record on commitments and good faith. López Obrador promised to determine the truth about Ayotzinapa but the investigation remained unresolved, independent experts withdrew, and military cooperation remained disputed. He promised greater transparency and described his government as highly transparent, while multiple assessments report declining access, inactive databases, military opacity, and weakened transparency institutions. He also stated that family members should not conduct business with government and issued a memorandum to that effect, but later reports allege continuing family and associate conflicts. There are countervailing implemented or attempted commitments, including investigative commissions, some access agreements, social and institutional reforms, and cooperation with selected international or domestic accountability processes.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0008-E009","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0009-E011","BATCH-0010-E011","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E016"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0012-E011","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not establish intent behind every policy change or distinguish all honest policy evolution from opportunistic reversal.","Several assessments concern administration-wide implementation rather than a specific formal promise made by the ruler."]},{"question_id":"7B.9","answer":"The shard reports allegations of favoritism and clientelism involving family friends, contractors, relatives, privileged access, and procurement. Reported examples include alleged simulated competition and contracts for associates of Andrés López Beltrán, specified-provider requirements linked to a friend, family-linked public contracts, discretionary government advertising, and protection or preferential treatment for military and political allies. López Obrador publicly defended relatives and denied corruption. The SFP found insufficient evidence in one conflict-of-interest investigation, and some official investigations and sanctions occurred, but the overall evidence describes incomplete accountability and repeated concerns about selective enforcement.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0006-E007","BATCH-0008-E007","BATCH-0008-E011","BATCH-0009-E008","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0008-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not prove López Obrador personally directed each contract, licensing decision, or enforcement action.","Many procurement and clientelism claims are allegations or investigative reporting rather than final audit or court findings."]},{"question_id":"7B.10","answer":"The shard predominantly describes conduct that weakened ethical example and public trust: repeated attacks and stigmatization of journalists, civil society, judges, investigators, and critics; denials or minimization of surveillance and investigative findings; alleged protection of military and political allies; weakened transparency and accountability institutions; and unresolved corruption, disappearance, and press-violence cases. These patterns are linked by several sources to normalization of impunity, opacity, polarization, and cynicism. Countervailing evidence includes election continuity, formal investigative institutions, some prosecutions and recovery efforts, court-led correction of executive measures, official apologies or remedies in selected cases, and reforms or international commitments. The shard therefore supports a materially mixed but adverse integrity environment, without by itself resolving the president’s personal responsibility for every institutional failure.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0003-E017","BATCH-0003-E019","BATCH-0004-E004","BATCH-0004-E007","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0007-E005","BATCH-0008-E009","BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0009-E005","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0009-E011","BATCH-0009-E012","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0010-E011","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0012-E009","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E016"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0012-E011","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E016"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Many cited indicators are country-wide or institutional and cannot independently establish personal ethical conduct.","The shard contains limited direct evidence of private conduct, asset disclosures, recusal, or durable personal integrity practices."]}],"cross_shard_cautions":["This shard is heavily concentrated on transparency, surveillance, Ayotzinapa, military accountability, press treatment, and family-conflict allegations; it provides little or no material evidence on some other integrity domains such as tax compliance, gifts, divestment, courts testimony, or appointments outside the reported cases.","Several records overlap the same underlying controversies and should not be treated as independent incidents without cross-shard deduplication.","Country-level repression, violence, corruption, and impunity evidence has been retained only where the supplied record identifies a ruler-specific statement, institutional direction, response, benefit, protection, tolerance, or accountability nexus; personal causation remains uncertain in many cases."]}
